description:
Speaker file upload fails on the deployed site with **"upload PUT network error"**.
Operator hit this on https://marquee.stage11.dev (2026-08-11) on the Presentation
Upload task. This blocks the file-upload step of the 11-step walkthrough loop —
the competition's evaluation rubric — so treat it as ship-blocking.

## Mechanism (traced, not guessed)

That exact string comes from `src/ui/upload/upload-client.ts:36`:

    xhr.onerror = () => reject(new Error("upload PUT network error"));

`xhr.onerror` fires only on a **browser-level** failure — DNS, TLS, or a blocked
CORS preflight. It does not fire for HTTP error statuses; `xhr.onload` handles
those and produces a different message ("upload PUT failed with status N"). So
the request never reached R2 as far as the browser is concerned.

The upload is a **direct browser PUT to R2**, cross-origin by construction:

- `src/lib/r2/presign.ts` signs against `https://{accountId}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/{bucket}/{key}`
  and deliberately refuses any other host.
- The page origin is `https://marquee.stage11.dev`. Different origin → preflight.
- The PUT is definitively **not** a CORS-simple request: `presignPut` requires
  `content-type` **and** `if-none-match: *`, and `upload-client.ts` attaches an
  `xhr.upload.onprogress` handler. Any one of those forces an `OPTIONS` preflight.
- **There is no CORS configuration anywhere in this repository.** A repo-wide search
  for `cors` / `AllowedOrigins` across `src/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, and
  `wrangler.jsonc` returns nothing. `wrangler.jsonc` binds the bucket
  (`MEDIA` → `marquee-media`) but a binding does not configure the S3 API's CORS
  rules, which is what a browser PUT is governed by.

Leading hypothesis: **the `marquee-media` bucket has no CORS policy**, so the
preflight is rejected and every browser upload fails. Note the implication —
this likely never worked on the deployed site. The suite is green because nothing
exercises a real cross-origin browser PUT; this is the textbook
"green tests ≠ working product" gap.

Rule out before fixing, in this order: (1) read the bucket's live CORS rules;
(2) check the browser console/network panel for the `OPTIONS` preflight and its
response; (3) only then look at the MRQ-89 bucket-scoped credential — a bad
credential returns **403**, which would surface as "failed with status 403", not
a network error. Do not assume MRQ-89; confirm from the preflight.

## Required outcome

1. **The bucket accepts browser uploads.** Apply a CORS policy to `marquee-media`
   (and the preview bucket if it serves any browser path) that allows `PUT` and
   `OPTIONS` from the site origin, with `content-type` and `if-none-match` in
   `AllowedHeaders` and `etag` exposed. Scope `AllowedOrigins` to the real origins
   — the production domain and whatever local dev origin the team uses. **Do not
   use `*`.**
2. **The policy is in the repo, not just in a dashboard.** A CORS rule that exists
   only as a console click is a rule that silently disappears on the next bucket
   rebuild and that no one can review. Commit the policy as a JSON file plus an
   idempotent apply script (wrangler or the S3 API), and document it in
   `code/platform/cloudflare.md` — see also `docs/` conventions in this repo.
3. **A test that would have caught this.** At minimum, an automated check that
   performs a real cross-origin `OPTIONS` preflight against the bucket and asserts
   the response allows `PUT` from the production origin. It does not belong in the
   45s fast suite — put it in the explicitly-invoked integration suite and wire it
   into the deploy check.
4. **The speaker-facing error stops being developer text.** "upload PUT network
   error" is an internal string in front of the least-equipped person to act on it.
   Replace the user-visible copy with a plain sentence and a retry, per the portal's
   own stated error philosophy (see the comment above `requestJson` in
   `PortalPage.tsx`). Keep the precise string in the console/logs for engineers.

## Constraints

- **Credentials never enter this repo.** It is going public. The apply script reads
  from the environment; the JSON policy file contains no secrets.
- Coordinate with MRQ-89's bucket-scoped credential — if the scoped token lacks the
  permission to *set* CORS, say so in the PR rather than widening the token silently.
- Suite budget 45s (this check goes in the slow suite), gate budget 120s.

## Acceptance

- On the **live deployed site**, signed in as a speaker, a real file uploads to
  completion on the Presentation Upload task — screenshot or recording in the PR
  showing the completed upload, plus the successful `OPTIONS` + `PUT` in the network
  panel. A green test alone does not close this ticket.
- The CORS policy is committed and re-appliable from a clean checkout by one command.
- `AllowedOrigins` is explicit; `*` appears nowhere.
- A deliberately wrong origin is still rejected (verify the policy is scoped, not open).
- The failure path shows a human sentence, not "upload PUT network error".
- PR open against `Stage-11-Agentics/marquee` `main`.
title: Upload is broken on the deployed site — presigned R2 PUT fails CORS preflight, no bucket policy exists
